messages:
Riley (oncall): noticing a huge spike in PD pages for inference-request-errors across multiple routes, starting ~00:12 UTC. Apps are degraded for some customers, overall 5xx rate up ~12x. paging me repeatedly.
OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT: inference-request-errors high (rate>100/min) · 00:12 UTC · triggered 8 services · severity: high · https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD12345
Riley (oncall): I'm on it. quick check: grafana shows error rate spike originates from /v1/generate and /v1/stream, all regions. latency also up.
Sam G: can we put a temporary PD dedupe / rate limit on the incident noise? it's drowning the oncall channel. suggest 5m dedupe window + aggregate grouping by service+region.
Chandra: agreed. also add short-lived alert threshold increase for the noisy rule while we investigate root cause. keep a metric-based guard so we don't hide legit incidents.
Alex P: I'll create a temporary squad-level suppression in PagerDuty (squelch) and set a routing rule to send only severity:critical pages. doing now.
PagerDuty Bot: Applying suppression: PD suppression id sup-789 created by Alex P · scope: service:(inference-api) · window: 10m · criteria: alert_type=="inference-request-errors"
Sam G: while Alex is doing that, can someone flip the dashboard to show per-model and per-route 1m bins? need to find whether it's a single model, a batching regression, or upstream client changes. Query I used:
```
sum by(route, model) (increase(inference_request_errors_total[1m]))
```
Riley (oncall): running the query now — looks concentrated on route=/v1/generate model=redwood-v2-small across eu-west-1. but there's also a smaller bump on /v1/stream.
Chandra: if it's model-specific, we can route traffic to a fallback variant (redwood-v2-med) in the smart routing layer to stop customer-facing errors while infra teams dig. that's faster than a full rollback.
Alex P: fallback routing from the console applied to EU region only. traffic split 80/20 to fallback. monitoring for error rate drop.
OpsBot: CONFIG CHANGE: routing policy updated · policy_id rp-456 · applied by Alex P · 00:25 UTC
Riley (oncall): error rate dropped ~70% after routing change and suppression. PD noise reduced but keep suppression active until root cause is fixed. I want a post-incident plan to reduce recurrence — probably need alert tuning and a new per-model dashboard.
SRE Lead: agree. action items: 1) temporary suppression + routing (done) 2) create a dedicated per-model error dashboard and add to oncall rota 3) tune alert thresholds: require sustained >3m for alert to fire; group by service+region+model 4) add PD dedupe window default for inference alerts to 5m 5) runbook update to include fallback routing steps.
Sam G: I'll open a Jira: INF-2987 "Alert tuning + per-model dashboard after PD cascade" and assign tasks. also proposing we add a PD rate-limit on low-severity pages at the global level.
Alex P: noted, Jira created INF-2987 · https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2987
Chandra: for the short term, let's make alert rules require >5 occurrences in 3m before page, and embed a quick link in the alert payload to the per-model grafana panel. helps faster triage.
Riley (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline at 01:20 UTC — Alex, can you watch suppression and routing for the next 2 hours? if errors recur escalate to SRE Lead.
Alex P: will monitor. set a reminder for 02:30 UTC to revisit settings and start rollback of suppression if stable.
OpsBot: REMINDER set by Alex P · 02:30 UTC · channel: eng-oncall
SRE Lead: after-action checklist: evaluate which alerts should be grouped (service+region+model) vs split; add rate-limits and dedupe defaults in PD; push a small dashboard patch to make per-model panels visible on the main oncall dashboard.
Riley (oncall): thanks team. leaving notes in the incident doc. will pick up post-mortem and alert-tuning PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
